title: HTML Forms Security
summary: Forms are the main attack surface of websites: they accept arbitrary user input, so everything submitted must be treated as hostile.
learningObjectives: Apply the concept in a small program
Predict program output by reading code

sections.content: Forms are the main attack surface of websites: they accept arbitrary user input, so everything submitted must be treated as hostile.

Defenses: CSRF tokens prove submissions came from your site, server-side validation checks types/ranges, output escaping prevents XSS, and HTTPS encrypts data in transit. Password fields should use autocomplete="new-password" hints and never log values.
Key points: client-side checks are UX only — the server must re-validate everything.

sections.codeExample:
<form method="post" action="/signup">
<input type="hidden" name="csrf" value="TOKEN">
<input type="email" name="email" required>
</form>
